articles.title: Alcaraz remonta para la historia a Shelton y repite final del Masters
articles.standfirst: El murciano se sobrepone a un set adverso a pesar de jugar físicamente diezmado
articles.summary: El murciano se sobrepone a un set adverso a pesar de jugar físicamente diezmado
articles.body: Por segundo año consecutivo, Carlos Alcaraz se plantado en la final de las ATP Finals bajo la condición de invicto. El murciano se ha impuesto este sábado en la primera semifinal a Ben Shelton, por 3-6, 6-3 y 7-6(1). Había perdido en el cara o cruz en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos y se tomó la revancha en otro gran escenario. Del 0-1 al 7-1. Para entender la dimensión de lo logrado por Carlitos basta con un dato estadístico. A sus 23 años, ha igualado las dos finales en el torneo que firmó Rafael Nadal en toda su carrera. El pupilo de Samuel López se planta en su trigésimo novena final. De momento, 29 títulos sobresalen en su palmarés. Y los dos últimos han sido en superficie dura bajo techo, un hábitat en el que encadena 14 victorias. El fenómeno de El Palmar está protagonizando el mejor regreso de la historia después de su lesión en la muñeca derecha que le tuvo cuatro meses y medio parado. Ha ganado 24 de los 26 partidos jugados, lo que da un porcentaje de efectividad del 92,30 por ciento. A cubierto, donde llegaba justo al 70 por ciento de éxito en sus apariciones, tiene ahora un 76,56. Shelton volvió a ser su víctima 13 días después de la final de París. El estadounidense cuenta con un enorme servicio, probablemente el mejor del circuito, pero le falta un esquema. Saber a lo que quiere jugar. Alcaraz firmó otra remontada épica, a pesar de estar físicamente limitado, tanto por su rodilla derecha como por el isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda. Ben se situó con un 3-0 arriba en la manga inicial, aprovechando la poca movilidad e intensidad en los apoyos del español, que iba con pies de plomo para no hacerse más daño del que ya tiene. Por precaución ha decidido entrenar lo justo antes de los partidos y calienta apenas 40 minutos antes de jugar. La nueva rutina surtió efecto con Cobolli, pero el saque de Ben necesita de algo más para poder ser restado. Gritaba Carlitos de desesperación, con un tanteo de 3-1 y 30-0. Ni la red estaba a su favor porque escupía sus tiros fuera. Devolverle un break a Shelton en dura es una misión casi imposible. Pero el líder de la Armada estaba dispuesto a intentarlo. Tenía que poner el escudo e intentar alargar los puntos. Su momento llegó, con 4-2, 15-40. El don al saque de su adversario no le permitió entrar en el partido. Con servicios a 227 kilómetros por hora todo es más fácil. Esa milésima tarde en impactar la pelota le costaba no precisar sus tiros con la precisión habitual. La seriedad entre los integrantes del banquillo era un reflejo de lo que estaba pasando. Ellos sabían mejor que nadie la situación en la que se encuentra su jugador. Alcaraz tomó por primera vez la delantera, con el 1-0 de la continuación. Shelton leía bien cuando tenía que sacar y subir. El segundo tren pasó con 2-1 y deuce. Un revés al pasillo de dobles y un misil de su rival le dejaron sin premio. Sin embargo, el campeón de siete grandes había afinado su maquinaría y amenazaba con la épica. El golpe sobre la mesa estaba al caer y este llegó en el octavo juego del segundo set. Su primera rotura le iba a permitir firmar las tablas en el marcador. Shelton empezaba sacando en la manga de desempate y eso es siempre una ventaja para él. Las fuerzas estaban muy justas y el desenlace estaba condenado al 'tie break'. El número tres mundial dejó para la videoteca un servicio a 219 km/h. Cada día que pasa en Turín está más cerca del cetro de maestro y más lejos de la Copa Davis de Bolonia.

articles.title: Alcaraz le recorta 5.590 puntos a Sinner en sólo seis torneos gracias a un 92,30 por ciento de victorias
articles.standfirst: El murciano está protagonizando el mejor regreso de la historia del tenis tras el percance en la muñeca
articles.summary: El murciano está protagonizando el mejor regreso de la historia del tenis tras el percance en la muñeca
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, flamante finalista de las ATP Finals 2026, está protagonizando el mejor regreso de la historia del tenis tras lesión. El murciano, que se perdió cuatro meses y medio de temporada por la lesión en la muñeca derecha que se produjo el 14 de abril, en la primera ronda del Godó con Otto Virtanen, firma un 92,30 de victorias desde que su vuelta al circuito en el US Open. En las pistas de Flushing Meadows, alcanzó los cuartos, donde fue derrotado por Ben Shelton, su víctima en la semifinal de Turín. Posteriormente, ganó su partido de la Laver Cup frente a Taylor Fritz. Completó la gira asiática con triunfo en Tokio y la tercera ronda de Shanghái. Como consecuencia de la suspensión del Six Kings Slam, Alcaraz pidió una invitación para jugar en Viena y se llevó el trofeo. Una semana después repetiría en el TMS de París. Este domingo disputará la final de la cita de maestros, con la opción de ganar su cuarto título en superficie dura bajo techo, que sería el tercer consecutivo. La regularidad en los resultados ha permitido al pupilo de Samuel López recortar 5.590 puntos a Jannik Sinner en apenas seis torneos. Podría terminar el curso a 350 puntos del italiano si se corona en el Masters masculino. El buen momento de Carlitos contrasta con el malo de Sinner, que se debate con pasar por el quirófano para solventar sus problemas en la rodilla derecha que no le han permitido jugar un partido desde el 12 de julio en Wimbledon.

articles.standfirst: El murciano repite final en la cita de maestros de Turín tras levantar un set a Shelton
articles.summary: El murciano repite final en la cita de maestros de Turín tras levantar un set a Shelton
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se mostraba orgulloso de sí mismo por la manera en la que está lidiando con todas las adversidades durante las ATP Finals de Turín 2026. El murciano volvió a realizar un ejercicio de escapismo ante Ben Shelton para acabar ganando en tres ajustados sets. Partido. "Hemos hecho puntos increíbles. Ha sido una batalla, cada vez que jugamos es una batalla, un gran show. La rivalidad con Ben no ha hecho más que empezar. Son los partidos que me hacen ser mejor jugador. He empezado con dudas y con errores y me ha servido gritar". Estado físico. "Mañana va a ser un día muy importante para mí y para mi equipo. Ahora empieza la recuperación física y mental. Voy a ir a ver a mi fisio (Juanjo Moreno). No he pensado en mi estado físico, simplemente he ido a por el partido. No era un momento para especular e ir con dudas. Lo que he intentado en el 'tie break' es hacer un buen tenis. S luego pierde haciendo las cosas bien, me voy de la pista satisfecho. Tenía que disfrutar del momento. Cuando estoy nervioso, quiero hacer más cosas de las que realmente tengo que hacer. Ha sido un gran test para entender dónde estoy a nivel físico. No me he empujado hasta el límite. No es necesario ir a todas las bolas". Ambición. "Ganar las ATP Finals siempre es un objetivo a principios de años. Espero ganar mañana, pero necesito descansar y veré la segunda semifinal". Tie break. "El 0-1 me ha hecho un saque que me ha dejado seco. Luego he sabido disfrutar de esa situación de nervios y él ha sentido la presión". Ganar el Masters. "Es uno de los torneos más importantes del calendario y mañana es la última bala y tiene que estar alineada". Presencia en la Copa Davis: "Aquí tengo partidos intensos físicamente y cada día que pasa tengo menos tiempo para ir a Bolonia y adaptarme a las circunstancias de allí".

articles.title: Thigh wrapped and knee taped, injury-hit Carlos Alcaraz digs deep to outlast Ben Shelton and reach ATP Finals
articles.summary: Despite carrying visible signs of discomfort, Carlos Alcaraz showed his fighting spirit and composure to book a place in the ATP Finals championship match.
articles.body: Despite carrying visible signs of discomfort, Carlos Alcaraz showed his fighting spirit and composure to book a place in the ATP Finals championship match. The Spaniard, who had his left thigh wrapped and tape on his right knee, recovered from a set down to beat American Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) in a gripping semifinal on Saturday.The seven-time Grand Slam champion extended his winning streak to 13 matches, overcoming a spirited challenge from the US Open runner-up to move within one victory of his maiden ATP Finals title.“It was a great battle,” Alcaraz said. “It was a great level from both of us the third set. Top games, top points, great highlights.”Alcaraz will face either world No. 1 Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev in Sunday's final. The two were scheduled to meet in the second semifinal later on Saturday.Alcaraz fights back to overcome SheltonShelton made an aggressive start, taking the initiative with some powerful shot-making. He produced an audacious swinging forehand volley winner in the opening game before breaking Alcaraz in the next, catching the Spaniard off guard with a forehand return winner.The American maintained his momentum to take the opening set 6-3, putting Alcaraz under pressure. However, the Spaniard gradually found his rhythm and raised his level in the second set.Alcaraz secured a crucial break late in the set and sealed it with a drop shot before producing a backhand passing winner to level the match.The deciding set turned into a closely fought contest, with both players producing some impressive tennis. When Shelton came up with a forehand drop volley midway through the set, Alcaraz responded with a thumbs-up, acknowledging the quality of the shot.Shelton held his serve for 5-4 with four aces, but Alcaraz took control in the tiebreak. Two consecutive aces and a couple of costly misses from the American helped the Spaniard race ahead 7-1 and seal the match on his first opportunity with a backhand return winner down the line.The victory also improved Alcaraz's head-to-head record against Shelton to 5-1. His only defeat against the American came in their memorable five-set US Open encounter earlier this year, which finished at 3:33 am.Injury concerns remain ahead of finalAlcaraz's victory came despite the physical concerns that have followed him through the tournament. He had injured his left hamstring during his group-stage match against Daniil Medvedev and has been managing his recovery since.“My recovery time is really important for me to recover my body, to recover mentally, to be prepared for tomorrow,” Alcaraz said.The Spaniard is chasing his first ATP Finals title after finishing runner-up to Jannik Sinner last year. Sinner, meanwhile, ended his season early because of a right knee injury. Alcaraz also faces a quick turnaround, with Spain set to compete in the Davis Cup Final 8 in nearby Bologna next week. However, he said he would assess his fitness on a day-to-day basis before deciding on his participation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Zverev y Alcaraz, una final de invictos en Turín con todo el botín en juego
articles.standfirst: El ganador sumará 1.500 puntos y se llevará un talón de 5.171.000 dólares
articles.summary: El ganador sumará 1.500 puntos y se llevará un talón de 5.171.000 dólares
articles.body: Por segundo año consecutivo, la final de las ATP Finals tendrá a dos protagonistas que llegan con la vitola de invictos. Carlos Alcaraz, que repite, contra Alexander Zverev. El mejor tenista del mundo de manera oficiosa frente al que lo es de forma oficial porque así lo dice el ranking ATP. El ganador se llevará todo el botín del Inalpi Arena: 1.500 puntos y 5.171.000 dólares. Alcaraz y Zverev han demostrado ser los mejores en Turín. Este sábado, horas después de que Carlitos pusiera el escudo para ganar a Ben Shelton, por 3-6, 6-3 y 7-6(1), Sascha superó a Daniil Medvedev, por 7-6(0) y 6-4. El alemán se convierte en el octavo tenista capaz de plantarse a la lucha por el título de maestro sin haber dejado escapar un set. Se une a un club en la que ya estaban Ilie Nastase, John McEnroe, Ivan Lendl, Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, Novak Djokovic y Jannik Sinner. El tenista de Hamburgo, campeón en las ediciones de 2018 y 2021, se agarra al hecho de que ha derrotado ya a Carlitos en seis ocasiones. Sólo Sinner ha ejercido más veces de verdugo del español. Sascha ha ganado en jerarquía este curso con sus dos Grand Slam, en Roland Garros y US Open, y su ascensión a lo más alto de las listas.

articles.summary: El murciano domina los precedentes entre ambos por siete victorias a seis
articles.body: Las ATP Finals 2026 tendrán la mejor final posible: Alexander Zverev (1) contra Carlos Alcaraz (3). Los dos primeros favoritos, por la ausencia de Jannik Sinner, que es segundo en el ranking, se han plantado este domingo en la lucha por el título. Alcaraz se deshizo en la primera semifinal de Ben Shelton mientras que Sascha acabó después con la resistencia de Daniil Medvedev, por 7-6(0) y De poco le sirvió al ruso tener el cara a cara ganado por 14 triunfos a ocho. El murciano domina los precedentes entre los dos finalistas por siete victorias a seis. El tenista de Hamburgo puede presumir de ser el segundo mayor verdugo de Carlitos en el circuito. Sólo Sinner (7) le ha vencido en más ocasiones. Zverev saldrá a jugar al Inalpi Arena de Turín con la confianza que le da su condición de número 1 ATP y doble campeón de un grande en el curso que ahora termina. La final de las ATP Finals entre Carlos Alcaraz y Alexander Zverev se disputará este domingo 22 en la pista central del Inalpi Arena de Turín, a partir de las 18:00 horas. Antes está previsto un mini concierto del cantante italiano Andrea Bocelli. La final de las ATP FInals, entre Carlos Alcaraz y Alexander Zverev, se podrá seguir a través de Movistar Plus, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición que reúne a los ocho mejores de la temporada. En MARCA.com y Radio MARCA habrá una amplia cobertura con la mejor información.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev gets his chance to silence critics against Carlos Alcaraz in ATP Finals final
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz will face Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals title clash on Sunday after both players won their semi-final matches in Turin.
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz will face Alexander Zverev in the ATP Finals title clash on Sunday after both players won their semi-final matches in Turin. Zverev defeated Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (0), 6-4, while Alcaraz came from a set down to beat US Open runner-up Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1).The final will give Zverev an opportunity to face Alcaraz on a major stage after facing criticism over his rise to the No. 1 ranking without beating either the Spaniard or Jannik Sinner. Zverev has also been criticised for not facing either player on his way to his first two Grand Slam titles.Alcaraz leads Zverev 7-6 in their career meetings. The Spaniard also won their only meeting this year, in the Australian Open semi-finals. Zverev, however, is looking forward to Sunday's contest after the two shared a practice session before the tournament.“We had a practice before the tournament started. It was unbelievable. We played one set for 1 ½ hours. So I hope it’s going to be similar tomorrow,” Zverev said. “I hope both of us are going to be at our best and hopefully it’s a really entertaining match for everybody.”Zverev is aiming to win his third ATP Finals title, while Alcaraz is chasing his first. The German has also faced a difficult record against Sinner, who has beaten him in their last 10 meetings. Sinner, however, ended his season early due to a right knee injury. He defeated Zverev in this year's Wimbledon final.Alcaraz manages thigh injury to reach finalAlcaraz had his left thigh wrapped and his right knee taped during his semi-final against Shelton. The Spaniard has been managing a left-thigh injury since Wednesday, but still managed to extend his winning run to 13 matches. The streak includes title wins in Vienna and Paris.The seven-time Grand Slam champion struggled to play with his usual freedom and lost the opening set before recovering to win in just over two hours. He also had to deal with a right wrist injury earlier this year, which kept him out of action for four-and-a-half months."I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning," said the seven-time Grand Slam winner."But I'm just happy that I came back in the second set... and ended up playing good tennis."Alcaraz lost to Sinner in last year's ATP Finals title match and will look to go one step further this time. Zverev, meanwhile, is seeking another title at the season-ending tournament, which features the year's top eight players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Career turning point: How Novak Djokovic’s 2010–2011 transformation shattered the Federer-Nadal duopoly and built a 16.8M-strong global following
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic’s journey from a struggling tennis player to one of the greatest champions in the sport began with a major change in 2010.
articles.body: Novak Djokovic’s journey from a struggling tennis player to one of the greatest champions in the sport began with a major change in 2010. Despite winning his first Grand Slam title at the 2008 Australian Open, the Serbian struggled with fitness problems that often affected his performances. However, a meeting with nutritionist Dr. Igor Četojević and a change in his eating habits helped him approach the game differently. What followed was a remarkable 2011 season, including 43 consecutive victories, his first Wimbledon title and his rise to world No. 1.What was holding Novak Djokovic back before his 2010 transformation?For several years, Djokovic struggled to maintain his fitness during long matches. Although he had the talent to challenge the best players, his physical problems often stopped him from playing at his highest level. Breathing difficulties, tiredness and struggles in hot conditions became regular concerns.His defeat to Austrian player Jürgen Melzer in the 2010 French Open quarterfinals was another difficult moment. Djokovic had won the first two sets but eventually lost the match in five sets. His inability to maintain his level over long matches remained a major concern as Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal continued to dominate men’s tennis.The turning point came during Serbia’s Davis Cup tie against Croatia in July 2010. Serbian nutritionist Dr. Igor Četojević noticed Djokovic’s physical struggles while watching him play and later contacted his team.According to Olympics.com, Četojević identified Djokovic’s sensitivity to gluten and dairy after examining his condition. This led to a major change in the Serbian’s eating habits.How did Dr. Igor Četojević change Novak Djokovic’s diet?Djokovic began following a gluten-free diet and also removed dairy products from his meals. He gradually changed what he ate, including avoiding foods that had been part of his regular diet growing up.The change was particularly significant because his family owned a pizzeria in Serbia, where bread and other wheat-based foods were part of everyday life.Djokovic later discussed the impact of this decision in his 2014 book, Serve to Win. He wrote:“Suddenly there was an X factor, a change in my diet that allowed my body to perform the way it was meant to.”The Serbian reported improvements in his energy levels and sleep after changing his diet. He also described feeling better during training and matches.It is important to note that his diet was one part of a wider change in his preparation. His fitness work, training, recovery and mental approach also played important roles in his development.The improvement soon became visible on the court, particularly during the final months of 2010 and the beginning of the following season.How did Novak Djokovic’s 2011 season end Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal’s dominance?Djokovic’s physical improvements came together with a major achievement for Serbian tennis in December 2010. He helped his country win its first Davis Cup title after beating France in the final in Belgrade.Playing in front of his home crowd, Djokovic won both his singles matches in straight sets. The victory gave him another reason to believe that he could compete with the best players in the world.He carried that confidence into the 2011 season and produced one of the most successful runs in tennis history.Djokovic won his first 41 matches of the 2011 season. When his two victories from the 2010 Davis Cup final were included, his overall winning streak reached 43 matches. His run ended against Federer in the French Open semifinals, where the Swiss defeated him in four sets.However, that defeat did little to slow Djokovic down for the rest of the season.He won the Australian Open, Wimbledon and US Open in 2011, finishing the year with three Grand Slam titles. His victories also changed the balance of power in men’s tennis.Djokovic defeated Nadal in six consecutive finals during the season, including at Wimbledon and the US Open. He also finished with a 4-1 record against Federer in 2011. His only defeat against the Swiss came in the French Open semifinals.The biggest personal milestone arrived at Wimbledon in July 2011. Djokovic defeated Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in the semifinals before beating Nadal in the final to win his first title at the tournament.That victory also took him to the top of the ATP rankings for the first time in his career. At that point, he was no longer just competing with Federer and Nadal. He had established himself as a serious force in men’s tennis.What records has Novak Djokovic achieved since his career transformation?The success of 2011 was not a short-lived run. Djokovic continued winning major titles and building records over the next decade, competing against several generations of players.His achievements include:Grand Slam titles: 24 men’s singles titles, the all-time record, including 10 Australian Open championships.Weeks at world No. 1: 428 weeks, the longest period at the top of the ATP rankings.Year-end No. 1 finishes: Eight, more than any other player in ATP history.ATP Masters 1000 titles: 40 titles, including winning all nine tournaments at least twice.ATP Finals: Seven titles, the most in the tournament’s history.Olympic gold: Won his first Olympic singles gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics after defeating Carlos Alcaraz in the final.His 24 Grand Slam titles also include three French Open, seven Wimbledon and four US Open championships.Djokovic has continued competing at the highest level even as he has entered the later stages of his career. He reached the 2026 Australian Open final, adding another major final appearance to his already remarkable record.According to the ATP Tour’s March 2026 records, he had also collected more than $197 million in career prize money. His ability to remain competitive after so many years on tour has made his fitness and recovery methods an important part of his career story.How has Novak Djokovic built a global following beyond tennis?Djokovic’s success has also helped him build a huge audience outside the tennis court. His achievements, personality and interactions with other players have made him one of the most recognisable names in international sport.His Instagram account, @djokernole, had approximately 16.8 million followers as of November 20, 2026, according to PicMany’s tracking data. This places him among the most followed tennis players on the platform.His social media content gives people a closer look at his life beyond professional matches. He shares training videos, fitness routines, family moments, celebrations and updates about his work through the Novak Djokovic Foundation.His Olympic gold medal celebration in Paris in 2024 was another major moment in his career. His interactions with younger players, including Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner, have also offered glimpses of his life away from the pressure of competition.From struggling with his fitness to holding some of the biggest records in tennis, Djokovic has built a career that reaches far beyond his Grand Slam victories.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "My daughter needed me at home": Naomi Osaka opened up about choosing daughter Shai over tennis before US Open
articles.summary: Naomi Osaka had spent years building a career around discipline, sacrifice and the relentless demands of professional tennis.
articles.body: Naomi Osaka had spent years building a career around discipline, sacrifice and the relentless demands of professional tennis. But before the 2026 US Open, the former world No. 1 made a decision that showed how much her priorities had changed since becoming a mother. While several of her rivals travelled to Cincinnati for another important hardcourt test, Osaka stayed home. The choice was not simply about managing fatigue or protecting her body. Her three-year-old daughter, Shai, needed her, and Osaka made it clear that tennis could wait.Naomi Osaka explained why daughter Shai came before the Cincinnati OpenOsaka had entered the North American hardcourt season with encouraging results. She reached the semifinals of the Mubadala DC Open before losing to eventual champion Alexandra Eala. She then advanced to the Canadian Open quarterfinals, where Elena Rybakina stopped her comeback bid with a 4-6, 7-6(5), 6-4 victory.Despite the demanding run, Osaka decided against playing the Cincinnati Open. She cited fatigue but later explained that her match schedule had already given her enough preparation for the final Grand Slam of the season.Her daughter's needs also shaped that decision. Osaka spoke candidly about the balance between her professional life and parenting, joking that tennis was almost a secondary occupation.“I mean, I do feel like I’ve played a lot of matches. And honestly, this is the surface that I’m most comfortable with, but I think people forget my main job is to be a mom. You know, this is like kind of my side hustle a little bit. I just happen to be really good at it. My daughter, she needed me to be at home, so that’s just what I felt like was the priority,” Osaka said.The remark offered a glimpse into the choices she faced as an elite athlete raising a young child. For Osaka, skipping one tournament was worth it if it meant being present when Shai needed her.Naomi Osaka did not want to decide her daughter's future in tennisOsaka also addressed whether she would encourage Shai to follow her into professional tennis. She did not dismiss the sport, recognising the lessons it had taught her throughout her career.“It’s not that I’m anti-tennis. I feel like it teaches you a lot and I think you know there’s a lot of characteristics that I gained through the sport. I think sports in general is really good for kids. It teaches discipline and all those other things,” she said.However, she wanted Shai to make that choice herself rather than grow up under expectations linked to her mother's success.“But I feel like for tennis I don’t know, maybe I’m stuck in my ways, but I think it can either go one of two ways. Like she’d really want to play professionally or maybe not, you know? I think those are things that I can’t control, but she loves swinging her little mini racket around. She actually hasn’t been on a real court yet. So maybe I’ll update you in a couple of years,” she added.Osaka entered the US Open as the No. 13 seed and was scheduled to face Anastasia Zakharova in the first round. After reaching the semifinals in New York the previous year, she hoped to make another deep run and pursue her first Grand Slam title since becoming a mother.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alexandra Eala has a message for her fans ahead of her exhibition match in the Philippines, ‘I am so excited’
articles.summary: Alexandra Eala has likely been enjoying a well-earned break from tennis of late, having played her last match of the season nearly two weeks ago...
articles.body:
Alexandra Eala has likely been enjoying a well-earned break from tennis of late, having played her last match of the season nearly two weeks ago now.

Her loss in the final of the Hong Kong Open marked a disappointing note to end on, but was indicative of what has been a hugely progressive campaign for the Filipina superstar.

She has gone from a player capable of great things but relatively inconsistent to a genuine threat to every player on the WTA Tour.

Alexandra Eala played more matches than any other player throughout 2026, and so will be seeking a rest more than most.

However, her break will be cut short when she returns to the Philippines to face Janice Then in an exhibition match in early December.

Now, speaking to reporters, she has a message for her fans as that date draws closer.

Alexandra Eala's message for fans ahead of playing a match in the Philippines

In a press conference shared by journalist Paige Javier, we got to see Eala answer two questions as she prepares to face her fellow Southeast Asian superstar in Manila.

She began with a brief overview of the match and how excited she is to be participating.

Eala claimed: "I think it's incredibly special to hold an event like this, you know, of this magnitude here.

"If you think about it, it will be only the second time that I have competed at this level here and one that's historic. You know, the sheer size of it will make it so much more intense, I think, and I'm so excited.

Then, asked if she had a message for her fans, the 21-year-old continued: "I would really, really love to have you guys and share in this super full circle and incredibly special moment that I can have here at home.

"To play here again after so many years against a really formidable player and a dear friend. It would mean the world to me if you guys can get a piece from that, and get a piece of how I feel and how proud I feel to be holding this event.

"So I hope to see you all on December 8th for my exhibition match."

Alexandra Eala finishes 2026 with a career-high ranking

Such a stunning season has seen Eala now nominated for an end-of-season WTA award , which is indicative of her progress across the last 11 months.

However, whether she wins that or not remains immaterial when compared to her new career-high ranking, achieved following her run in Hong Kong.

She is now confirmed to finish the year ranked 15th in the world, just above Naomi Osaka, and just below her good friend Iva Jovic.

Eala's prize money for 2026 has also taken a huge upturn, marking another benefit to her fine form and newfound consistency.

articles.title: Who needs to win ATP Finals more: Carlos Alcaraz or Alexander Zverev?
articles.summary: Both want to win, but who needs the win more?
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev will face off for the 2026 ATP Finals trophy in Turin, Italy on Sunday, November 22.

Alcaraz has never won the ATP Finals. Zverev is a two-time champion, defeating Novak Djokovic in 2018 and Daniil Medvedev in 2021.

Who needs to win the 2026 ATP Finals more?

Alcaraz, the 2026 Australian Open champion, is coming off a bizarre season. He spent over 4 1/2 months recovering from a wrist injury. He returned for the US Open and has gained form late in the season.

In Turin, Alcaraz is wearing knee tape and a wrap around his hamstring so it is not clear how close he is to 100%.

Zverev has won this event twice. He has stayed relatively healthy throughout the season, winning two Grand Slams and assuming the World No. 1 ranking for the first time.

With Jannik Sinner out, the ATP Finals is getting its dream matchup of the two best players of the 2026 season.

No matter what people say about Zverev's 2026 season, he is the undisputed ATP Player of the Year, regardless of what happens in Sunday's final.

Alcaraz has accomplished a lot in his tennis career, but winning the ATP Finals is uncharted territory. The win would also tie him with Sinner at 30 career ATP titles. Alcaraz is 7-6 head-to-head against Zverev. For these reasons, it is more important for Alcaraz to lift the ATP Finals trophy on Sunday in Turin.

articles.standfirst: El seleccionado nacional habla de la opción de que Carlitos juegue el dobles con Granollers
articles.summary: El seleccionado nacional habla de la opción de que Carlitos juegue el dobles con Granollers
articles.body: Después de cuatro años en el cargo de seleccionador nacional, David Ferrer se despide del banquillo en la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 a 29). Ferru habla con MARCA antes del debut del próximo jueves contra Austria y desgrana la importancia de la presencia de Carlos Alcaraz, al que ve en los individuales y en el dobles. Pregunta. Usted tenía un año más de contrato con la Federación. ¿Cuándo y por qué decide dejar la capitanía de la Copa Davis? Respuesta. Al empezar el año tenía ya esa incertidumbre porque me habían venido jugadores para ver si les podía entrenar. Creía que era el momento, que mi ciclo como capitán había terminado este año y me apetecía volver a viajar y tener otras oportunidades. No quería esperar mucho más y pensaba que era el momento adecuado. He estado cuatro años en el cargo y yo creo que tiene que ser algo cíclico lo de ser capitán de la Copa Davis. Lo de Casper (Ruud) me llegó a mitad de esta temporada y pensándolo bien es un proyecto bonito para empezar de nuevo. P. Ferrero comenta que su estilo de tenis y el de Ruud son parecidos y que funcionarán juntos. R. No lo sé, es difícil de decir. Creo mucho en el proyecto, pero todavía soy capitán de Copa Davis y es lo más importante ahora mismo. Lo que me convenció de Casper es su entorno. Todos están alineados en lo que son los valores y a nivel profesional. P. ¿La Copa Davis que usted ha vivido como seleccionador es muy distinta a que vio como tenista? R. Sí, es muy diferente. Todo evoluciona y todo cambia y la Copa Davis ha cambiado. En los últimos años ha habido muchos cambios en el formato. P. ¿Ha perdido un poco el atractivo y el prestigio para los jugadores? R. Está claro que cuando ganas la Copa Davis te hace mucha ilusión porque juegas para tu país. Pero es cierto que la Copa Davis ahora no es una prioridad para los jugadores como lo era antes para Feliciano, Rafa Nadal o para mí. El formato era distinto y no había tantas competiciones. Una de las cosas que quema mucho a la Copa Davis es que prácticamente todos los Masters 1000 sean de dos semanas. Eso hace que los jugadores, por tema de calendario, lleguen mermados físicamente. Yo creo que eso ha hecho bastante daño. P. ¿Acepta el cartel de favoritos o hay más favoritos aparte de España? R. Lo acepto. Hay más candidatos, pero nosotros somos uno de los principales favoritos. Es algo obvio, no pasa nada. Después podremos ganar o perder. En Málaga también éramos favoritos, cuando Rafa estuvo con nosotros, y perdimos contra un equipo como el de Holanda, que a priori fue una sorpresa que llegara a la final. La realidad es que si están los jugadores sanos y pueden estar en Bolonia tanto Carlos como Rafa y Marcel somos favoritos. No pasa nada por decirlo. Eso es como cuando en un torneo están Alcaraz y Sinner. Ganarán o perderán, pero ellos son los favoritos. P. Alcaraz, Jódar y Granollers se clasificaron para las ATP Finals. ¿Es un arma de doble filo por el riesgo a lesionarse? R. Sí, eso nos pasó el año pasado con Carlos y fue una pena porque él es fundamental para nosotros, es clave. Pero yo me alegro de que haya tres españoles jugando el Masters. Eso significa que el tenis español va muy bien y que tenemos buenos jugadores. Lo prefiero a tener a tenistas que no han hecho Masters y no tengan esa confianza de ganar tantos partidos. Yo lo intento mirar desde la parte positiva. Alcaraz no ha jugado tantos torneos y Rafa ha jugado mucho, pero tiene una ilusión enorme. Y Marcel no me preocupa tanto porque en el dobles no hay un desgaste físico muy grande. P. En caso de que una serie vaya empate a uno, ¿se plantea la opción de juntar a Granollers con Alcaraz? R. Sí, claro. Si Carlos está bien tiene muchas posibilidades de jugar el dobles. P. ¿Levantar la Davis sería la despedida soñada? R. Soñada no sería la palabra, pero sí que sería la despedida perfecta. Has hecho un trabajo durante tres años y muchas veces no ha sido sencillo convocar a todos los jugadores importantes. Vamos a tocar madera. Pase lo que pase no va a cambiar nada. Yo estoy contento del trabajo y de la oportunidad. Lo he intentado hacer lo mejor que he podido y, en este aspecto, me voy tranquilo. Tuve la suerte de irme tranquilo de todos los trabajos que he tenido. He dado todo lo que tenía que dar, he dado el máximo de mí. P. ¿Le ha sorprendido el salto de Rafa Jódar en tan poco tiempo? R. Yo sabía que era un grandísimo jugador porque ya lo tuve de sparring en la Copa Davis. Pero sí que nos ha sorprendido que empezó el año muy por detrás en el ranking y ahora sea top10 y juegue el Masters. Sabíamos que iba a estar arriba, pero que lo haya hecho en un año ha sido una barbaridad, sin lugar a dudas. Me alegro por él. P. ¿Marc López es un relevo natural en la capitanía? R. Sí, yo creo que la federación lo ha hecho muy bien en este aspecto. Primero porque está capacitado, conoce el entorno, a los jugadores, los jugadores le conocen a él. Me alegro por Marc y creo que la federación ha hecho bien apostando por una continuidad de las cosas que están funcionando. P. ¿Cuál será su primer torneo al lado de Casper Ruud? R. Empezaré a principios de año, en el Open de Australia voy a estar seguro. P. ¿Cómo ve la unión entre Juan Carlos Ferrero y Ben Shelton? R. Lo veo bien. Es un jugador joven, con mucha proyección, está el cuatro del mundo y es candidato a ganar Grand Slam. Juan Carlos le ayudará mucho sobre todo en el tema del esquema de juego. Creo que, junto a su padre Bryan, harán un buen tándem. Veo a Juan Carlos muy ilusionado y eso es lo más importante, Voy a tener la suerte de coincidir con él en el circuito y en los últimos años no hemos podido hacerlo.

articles.standfirst: El murciano calentará a las 17:00 horas y el partido decisivo está programado a las 18:00
articles.summary: El murciano calentará a las 17:00 horas y el partido decisivo está programado a las 18:00
articles.body: No hay que cambiar lo que está funcionando. Eso es un lema que aplica Carlos Alcaraz y los miembros de su equipo. Esa es la razón por la que, por tercer día consecutivo, según ha podido saber MARCA, el tenista calentará escasamente 60 minutos antes de saltar a la pista a disputar la final de las ATP Finals con Alexander Zverev. El campeón de siete grandes tiene reservada la pista a las 17:00 horas y la lucha por la corona de maestro está programada a las 18:00. Carlitos empezó a realizar esta rutina exprés el viernes en el último partido de la fase de grupos contra Flavio Cobolli para preservar al máximo su condición física tras sentir algo en el isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda el miércoles en el primer juego del segundo set con Daniil Medvedev. Apareció en la pista Sebastopoli, pegada a la central del Inalpi Arena, con un margen de 45 minutos. Fueron 40 en la previa de la semifinal con Ben Shelton. Y es que el descanso y la recuperación son ahora mismo la prioridad de Alcaraz, que ya tiene de sobras rodaje de juego y ritmo de competición. Gran parte del éxito del fenómeno de El Palmar en Turín hay que dárselo a su equipo, empezando por su fisioterapeuta Juanjo Moreno y sus manos mágicas. El tenista tenía prisa ayer para terminar todos sus compromisos posteriores a la semifinal con Shelton porque cada minuto en la camilla es oro para afrontar con plenas garantías la final del torneo de maestros con Zverev. "Vamos a hacer y vamos a usar cada minuto y cada hora del día para recuperar, para hacer las cosas bien y estar lo mejor posible”, se sinceraba el flamante finalista. Carlitos juega por la historia del tenis masculino español, que no se corona en la cita de los ocho mejores desde la edición de 1998 con Álex Corretja. Antes había ganado Manolo Orantes, en 1976.

articles.title: Alcaraz ofrece una clase magistral ante Zverev y España tiene maestro 28 años después
articles.standfirst: El murciano derrota al alemán en dos sets y es el tercer español que gana las ATP Finals tras Orantes y Corretja
articles.summary: El murciano derrota a
articles.body: Los 13.500 espectadores que llenaban hasta los topes el Inalpi Arena de Turín, una majestuosa construcción inaugurada para los Juegos Olímpicos de 2006, siempre podrán decir que han visto jugar y han visto ganar a Carlos Alcaraz. El murciano, coleccionista de siete títulos del Grand Slam, ya tiene el cetro de maestro ATP tras superar en la final a Alexander Zverev, por 6-2 y 7-6(7). Su recital estuvo a la altura de su telonero, el compositor local, Andrea Bocelli. El tenis masculino español había tenido que esperar 28 años para encontrarle un relevo a Álex Corretja, vencedor en la edición de 1998 celebrada en Hannover. Antes que él se había impuesto Manolo Orantes, en 1976, en Houston. En la capital de la región del Piamonte Alcaraz ejercía de local. “Me siento muy querido cada vez que vengo aquí. Me encanta jugar delante de ellos porque son muy apasionados por el tenis”, reconoce. Carlitos les da argumentos para vibrar y de qué manera. Su quinto recital le permite vencer invicto y llevarse el botín de 1.500 puntos y 5.151.000 dólares. Releva en el palmarés a Jannik Sinner, que queda por detrás de él en el ranking histórico de ganancias. Por delante están Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal, Roger Federer y el derrotado Zverev. El pupilo de Samuel López firma el mejor regreso de siempre tras una lesión de muñeca que le alejó cuatro meses y medio de la competición oficial. De sus 30 títulos, cuatro de ellos han llegado en apenas 55 días. Ya son 15 victorias seguidas en superficie dura bajo techo, la que se ha convertido en su nuevo jardín gracias a las mejoras técnicas en su juego y, en especial, en el saque. “Me mato con el saque en el tercer set”, advertía Ben Shelton tras perder la semifinal. Su verdugo ha pasado más tiempo firmando autógrafos delante de su hotel, Principe Di Piemonte, que calentando antes de los partidos. En los últimos tres, la sesión preparatoria se redujo a la mínima expresión y una hora antes de saltar a pista. A Alcaraz le daba tiempo de pasar por la ducha, recolocar la diadema del pelo y jugar. La prioridad era la recuperación física. El nuevo maestro ha podido con todos los contratiempos posibles. Ha lucido desde el primer día un estabilizador rotuliano en la rodilla derecha, tuvo que parar el tercer entreno en Turín por un problema estomacal y el pasado miércoles sintió algo en el isquiotibial que le obligó a pasar consulta y hacerse una resonancia magnética para cerciorarse de que no tenía una rotura muscular. Alcaraz ya disfrutó de tres pelotas de break en el juego inicial. Metía toda la presión del mundo a su rival desde la devolución. Es por eso que Sascha recibió un 'warning' por retrasar el servicio nada más empezar. En el momento de presión el actual número 1 mundial siempre falla por la derecha, sobre todo con bolas blandas, y es una lección que tiene Samu más que aprendida. El vencedor rompió en blanco en el tercer parcial. "Anímate", le decía su preparador cuando Zverev volvía a la carga inmediatamente después con tres pelotas de rotura. Las salvó con el temple de los elegidos. "Atrévete, segundo directo", le insistían desde el banquillo. El murciano repitió ofensiva en el quinto juego. El perdedor pedía explicaciones a Alexander senior, padre a la vez que técnico. Carlitos levitaba en los descansos al ritmo de la música que pinchaba un DJ venido para la ocasión. El alemán logró su rotura, pero no le dio para remontar el primer parcial porque estaba jugando con un tenista de otro planeta, capaz de ejecutar un entrepiernas y convertirlo en un globo ganador. Zverev, contrariado, lanzó la raqueta. Las 14 veces que bota la bola antes del saque le costaron una advertencia por la que perdió un servicio. Fue la antesala del tercer break del campeón de siete grandes. La sentencia pudo llegar el séptimo juego del segundo set. Alcaraz disfrutaba de un 4-3 y saque. Su adversario gastó su última vida para darle la vuelta a esa situación de máxima presión y restar para firmar las tablas en el marcador con un 0-30. Cuando más quema la bola, pues se inventó una dejada. El desenlace moriría en la muerte súbita y Sascha se fabricaría tres pelotas de segunda manga. Del 3-6 al 6-6, con una dejada, un remate y un tiro del teutón al pasillo. Se le escapó la primera bola de maestro, con una derecha larga. No fallaría en la segunda. Carlitos es el vigésimo séptimo tenista en levantar el cetro de maestro y el cuarto que lo hace además con todos los majors, junto a Andre Agassi, Roger Federer y Novak Djokovic.

articles.title: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz beats world No 1 Alexander Zverev in blockbuster final to claim title for first time
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz joins Andre Agassi , Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic as the only players to win a career Grand Slam and the ATP Finals title; Alcaraz defeated Alexander Zverev in straight sets to win the season finale for the first time
articles.body:
Alcaraz dominated at times as he defeated Zverev 6-2 7-6 and became just the fourth man with a career Grand Slam and the ATP Finals title, following on from Andre Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic .

Zverev won the first two Grand Slam titles this year but ends his breakout season having failed to beat Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner, with the German falling short in his bid to win the ATP Finals for a third time.

Alcaraz played with heavy strapping on his left leg but moved freely during his victory, which came in just over two hours and continued his 100 per cent record in finals against Zverev.

The 23-year-old dropped just two sets during his 14-match winning streak, with ATP Finals victory following titles at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters and earning him a winner's prize of nearly $5.2m.

How Alcaraz beat Zverev to ATP Finals title

Zverev hadn't dropped his serve all week but Alcaraz tested him from the start, earning three break points in the opening game of the match. He saved all three of those - one of them with an ace after receiving a time violation warning - only for Alcaraz to break him in his next three service games.

When Alcaraz produced a "tweener" - a shot between his legs - to recover a lob midway through the first set and Zverev missed the ensuing overhead, he threw his racket angrily toward the baseline.

Zverev again took too long and was docked his first serve, prompting him to complain to the chair umpire, while Alcaraz controlled by stretching the German from corner to corner and breaking again early in the second set.

Alcaraz pulled off an acrobatic, leaping overhead as he was falling backward, putting his finger to his ear to encourage more cheering from the crowd, with the match appearing for a quick finish before Zverev broke back to make it 4-4 in the second set.

Zverev wasted three set points in the tie-breaker before Alcaraz converted his second match point with a backhand winner up the line, then dropped to the court on his back in celebration.

Alcaraz: ATP Finals win 'means the world'

Alcaraz is the third Spaniard to win the ATP Finals, following on from Manuel Orantes in 1976 and Alex Corretja in 1998, capping off a memorable campaign where he also became the youngest player to complete the career Grand Slam.

"For me it's been an amazing week," Alcaraz said. "I couldn't have ended the week in a better way. I'm just really proud and really happy with everything I have done this week.

"I've been through really difficult moments within myself, with my team, and we went through everything playing great tennis. This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me."

Alcaraz has also significantly closed the gap to world No 2 Sinner in the PIF ATP Rankings, moving with 350 points of the 2025 champion after entering the week 1,850 points behind.

"You're an absolute legend of our sport and you're only 23 years old," Zverev said during his runner-up speech. "If you retire tomorrow, it's okay, you can just relax."

articles.summary: El murciano y el italiano empatan a 30 títulos, seis en 2026, que son 17 en los grandes escenarios del deporte de la raqueta
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha aprovechado la ausencia de Jannik Sinner para darle caza en varias estadísticas en la carrera por entrar en el club de los mejores de la historia. El murciano, que ha reducido en 6.090 puntos la diferencia en el ranking con Sinner desde su regreso a la competición en el pasado US Open (finaliza el curso a 350 puntos), ha igualado este domingo los 30 títulos del italiano en el circuito y los seis del curso que ahora termina. De igual forma, empata con el italiano en grandes coronas. Eso contempla los cuatro Grand Slam, los nueve Masters 1000 y las ATP Finals. Carlitos y Jannik suman 17, repartidas de la siguiente manera. El pupilo de Samuel López tiene siete 'majors', nueve TMS y la cita de maestros de 2026. articles.standfirst: El tenista de El Palmar aspira a unirse a un histórico club en el que sólo están Andre Agassi y Novak Djokovic
articles.summary: El tenista de El Palmar aspira a unirse a un histórico club en el que sólo están Andre Agassi y Novak Djokovic
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, a sus 23 años y 201 días, está más cerca de unirse a dos leyendas como Andre Agassi y Novak Djokovic, los únicos que pueden presumir de haber ganado todos los grandes títulos del tenis. Agassi y Djokovic inscribieron su nombre en el palmarés de los cuatro Grand Slam, conquistaron la corona de maestros ATP, levantaron la Copa Davis por su país y se colgaron el oro olímpico en categoría individual. En esa misión se encuentra Alcaraz, que ya ha vencido una vez en el Open de Australia (2026); dos en Roland Garros (2024 y 2025); otras dos en Wimbledon (2023 y 2024); y otras tantas en el US Open (2022 y 2025). Cabe recordar que el pasado mes de enero, en las pistas del Melbourne Park, se convirtió en el más precoz en completar el Grand Slam. Carlitos ya tiene el Masters masculino, tras derrotar a Alexander Zverev, y le quedan por conseguir la máxima competición por países y el oro en los Juegos. En los últimos de París se quedó a las puertas tras perder la final con Djokovic. El hándicap para él en la próxima cita olímpica de Los Ángeles 2028 es que la competición se inicia tres días después de concluir Wimbledon y para subir a lo más alto del podio hay que ganar seis partidos, que se sumarían a los siete del grande de la hierba. La superficie de juego en la ciudad californiana será de cemento. Alcaraz está convocado para la fase final de la Copa Davis 2026 en Bolonia. La selección debuta el jueves 26 contra Austria y viaja este lunes a la ciudad italiana para levantar la Ensaladera. De momento, se ha convertido en el cuarto en poseer los cuatro Grand Slam y las ATP Finals, junto a Agassi, Djokovic y Federer.

articles.title: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz beats world number one Alexander Zverev to claim title
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz ends his wait for a first ATP Finals title as he outplays world number one Alexander Zverev in Turin.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz outplayed world number one Alexander Zverev to end his wait for a first ATP Finals title and complete a remarkable post-injury return to the sport.

A season which began with Alcaraz becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, before he was ruled out for more than four months with a wrist issue, ended with the Spaniard holding aloft another of the sport's biggest trophies.

Alcaraz, still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following his injury scare earlier in the week, collapsed to the ground in celebration after sealing a 6-2 7-6 (9-7) win in a dramatic second-set tie-break.

It was a statement victory over Zverev, who took advantage of Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's injury absences to rise to the top of the rankings and claim his first two major titles.

It was a 14th successive win and a third-straight title triumph for seven-time major winner Alcaraz, who demonstrated beyond any doubt that he is back to his devastating best.

"Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time, it means the world to me," the 23-year-old said.

"I have been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team. For me it's been an amazing week.

"I couldn't finish the week in a better way."

Alcaraz ends long wait for ATP Finals glory

It is just 84 days since Alcaraz made his return at the US Open in August after a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Since that tournament, the current world number three has won 21 of his 22 matches and swept titles at four of the five tournaments he has entered.

With his latest victory, Alcaraz has become the youngest man to win all four Grand Slams and the season-ending Finals - and only the fourth in history.

Zverev, who ends 2026 with an ATP Tour-leading 69 match victories, had not dropped serve in four straight-set matches to reach the final.

But for much of the two-hour title decider, his greatest weapon was dismantled by a brilliant Alcaraz.

Alcaraz handled the occasion far better as he emerged from a tense start with a 4-1 double-break lead on his way to the first set.

The contrasting emotions of the two players were evident when Alcaraz wore a big grin after pulling off a between-the-legs lob that Zverev smashed into the net. At the other end of the court, the German threw away his racquet in disgust.

While Alcaraz danced to music during a change of ends, Zverev's frustrations only grew as, after winning back one of the two breaks of serve, he received a second time violation on his way to losing serve for a third successive game.

The top seed left the court after unravelling in the first set, having produced just three winners to 19 unforced errors in an inconsistent start.

Alcaraz's march to the title appeared inevitable as he took control of the second set with a fourth break of serve, but Zverev restored parity in the eighth game and kept his hopes alive by forcing a tie-break.

Overturning a 3-0 deficit in the tie-break, Zverev then won six straight points to arrive at three set points.

However, he failed to take all of them, including one on his own serve, before Alcaraz drove in a backhand winner on his second match point.

After picking himself off the floor, the Spaniard celebrated with his team in the stands after finally landing the title he had been chasing for four years.

In the doubles, French debutants Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti lifted the trophy after a comeback victory against Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic.

The sixth seeds recovered from losing the first set to win 3-6 7-6 (7-2) 10-6, ending the year with the most wins (59) and titles (seven) in men's doubles.

articles.standfirst: Recorrerá en coche los 331 kilómetros que separan Turín de la sede de la fase final de la máxima competición por países
articles.summary: Recorrerá en coche los 331 kilómetros que separan Turín de la sede de la fase final de la máxima competición por países
articles.body: La final de las ATP Finals, entre Carlos Alcaraz y Alexander Zverev, puede repetirse el próximo sábado 28 en las semifinales de la Copa Davis. España y Alemania, que circulan por el mismo lado del cuadro, podrían cruzarse en unas hipotéticas semifinales si vencen antes a Austria y Gran Bretaña, respectivamente. Es el único gran título que le falta a Sascha en su palmarés, en el que hay Grand Slam, Masters 1000, ATP Finals, el oro olímpico y el cetro de número 1 del circuito masculino. Alcaraz, según ha podido saber MARCA, tiene previsto desplazarse este lunes a Bolonia, sede de la fase final de la máxima competición por países. El trayecto de 331 kilómetros lo realizará en coche, a primera hora de la tarde, junto a su entrenador Samuel López. Por normativa de la Federación Española de Tenis, los tenistas convocados sólo pueden ir acompañados de una persona y se aconseja que sea el técnico. Carlitos descansará a su llegada al hotel Royal Carlton de Bolonia y a las 18:30 horas estará en la rueda de prensa oficial de la selección nacional, previa al debut del jueves contra Austria. Los convocados por parte de David Ferrer se han ido incorporando de manera escalonada. Marcel Granollers, procedente de Turín, y Dani Mérida, fueron los dos primeros en llegar el sábado. A última hora se incorporó Rafa Jódar. Este lunes se espera a Carlitos, el indiscutible líder de la Armada. Para encontrar al última tenista que hizo doblete en las ATP Finals y la Copa Davis hay que remontarse a Jannik Sinner, en 2024. Alcaraz va a por ello con todo.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz adds ATP Finals title to glittering trophy cabinet
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz made more history with a maiden ATP Finals title after a straight-sets win over Alexander Zverev. A 6-2 7-6 (7) triumph in Turin enabled seven...
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz made more history with a maiden ATP Finals title after a straight-sets win over Alexander Zverev.

A 6-2 7-6 (7) triumph in Turin enabled seven-time major champion Alcaraz to follow in the footsteps of Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic by becoming the fourth male player to win the end-of-season tournament along with each four grand slams in their career.

Alcaraz had finished runner-up to Jannik Sinner in 2025 and lost twice to current world number one Zverev previously in the competition, but showed why many still proclaim the Spaniard to be the best player in the world after an impressive two-hour-and-two-minutes victory.

With strapping on his left leg and after a gruelling three-set battle with Ben Shelton on Saturday, Alcaraz set about becoming the first player of the week to take a set off French Open and US Open champion Zverev.

Top seed Zverev was forced to dig deep to hold on his first service game, but was broken three times during a one-sided opening set.

Alcaraz broke again to move 2-1 up in the second before a 4-2 lead was established.

However, Alcaraz let slip his advantage and a topsy-turvy tie-break followed between the first and second seed.

After Alcaraz claimed an early break, Zverev reeled off six points in a row, but failed to take three set points.

Then at the second time of asking, after one match point was saved, Alcaraz produced a bullet backhand to defeat Zverev and he duly collapsed to the ground after winning the 30th title of his extraordinary career and sixth of an injury-hit 2026.

"This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me," Alcaraz said on-court.

"Today's final, I needed to put the three c's that my grandpa always tells me that I have to give every time that I step on the court for every match and every practice.

"He's watching at home, so I just want to say I love you to my grandparents. In Spanish it's 'Cabeza, corazon, cajones', in English it is 'head, heart, balls', so I think today that was about it."

articles.title: Alcaraz y su pensamiento en el suelo: "Pedí, por favor, que la bola hubiera entrado"
articles.standfirst: El murciano reconoce la importancia de su equipo en la consecución del título
articles.summary: El murciano reconoce la importancia de su equipo en la consecución del título
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz no se separó en ningún momento del trofeo de maestro ATP. Primero en la pista, inmortalizándose con sus familiares y equipo, y después en la rueda de prensa. Trabajo del equipo con Samuel López y su hermano Álvaro. "Me pusieron las cosas muy fáciles durante el tiempo en el que estuve lesionado. Me di cuenta lo importante que es para mí sentirme bien fuera de la pista en mi vida para ir a los entrenos hambriento y con motivación. Todas las cosas que me decían eran en positivo y me ayudó mucho. Esto no ha hecho más que empezar". Mejor tenista del momento. "No me siento el mejor. Todo el mundo se siente el número 1. Yo, Sascha, Jannik, Shelton... Todos se lo creen. Y creo que tener esa confianza es muy importante cuando vas a entrenar o entras a la pista. La realidad es que el número 1 del ranking es ahora mismo Sascha y lo merece. Nadie se lo va a quitar". Tumbado en la pista. "Cuando estaba en el suelo lo primero que he pensado es que no cantaran mi golpe fuera porque a veces el ojo de halcón va con retraso. Pensaba: 'por favor, que la bola haya sido dentro'". Título. "Es un torneo que tenía muchas ganas de ganar algún día. Estaba persiguiendo ese momento desde hace mucho tiempo. Fueron dos semanas muy difíciles para mí lidiando con la presión, con problemas físicos, con reuniones de equipo para tomar decisiones, controlándome dentro y fuera de la pista..." Sentimiento por ser maestro del tenis. "Significa muchísimo. Este trofeo es algo increíble para mí, para mi equipo y para mi familia. Ellos saben lo importante que era este torneo para mí. Todo lo que haces durante el año es para poder clasificarte para estar aquí. Luego llegas a Turín y juegas cinco partidos con los ocho mejores del mundo. El año pasado me quedé muy cerca de ganar y esta vez veníamos con mucha ambición, con muchas ganas. Ha sido una semana muy difícil porque he tenido que lidiar con muchas situaciones fuera de pista. Acabar de esta manera es algo increíble y vamos a disfrutarlo". Copa Davis. "La Copa Davis es algo muy importante para mí y vamos a ir para allá. Intentaré dar lo mejor de mí y ayudar al equipo lo máximo que podamos ya que va a ser una semana muy bonita y a la que le tengo muchas ganas".

articles.title: El bonito mensaje de Nadal a Alcaraz tras ganar las ATP Finals: "Sé de verdad que ha sido un año complicado..."
articles.standfirst: El balear felicita al murciano por ganar precisamente el único gran torneo que falta en su increíble palmarés
articles.summary: El balear felicita al murciano por ganar precisamente el único gran torneo que falta en su increíble palmarés
articles.body: Entre las muchas felicitaciones que está recibiendo Carlos Alcaraz por su victoria en las ATP Finals destaca sin duda alguna la de Rafa Nadal. El ex tenista balear, nuevo directivo del Real Madrid, ha escrito un bonito y emotivo mensaje en las redes sociales felicitando a su compatriota y compañero en el dobles de los Juegos Olímpicos de París 2024. "¡Enhorabuena Carlos Alcaraz por ganar las ATP Finals! Sé de verdad que ha sido un año complicado y me alegro muchísimo de que hayas podido ganar este torneo tan importante y jugando tan bien. ¡Suerte ahora en la Davis!", escribió Rafa en su cuenta de Twitter. Alcaraz se ha convertido hoy en el tercer español en levantar este trofeo tras Manuel Orantes y Alex Corretja. Nadal llegó a disputar dos finales pero perdió ante Roger Federer, en 2010, y frente a Novak Djokovic, en 2013. Se trata precisamente del único gran trofeo que no está en las vitrinas de Rafa, que sí puede presumir de 22 grandes, dos oros olímpicos, uno individual (Pekín 2008) y otro en dobles (Río 2016), y cinco Copa Davis. Es significativo que Rafa mande precisamente ánimos a Carlitos de cara a la cita de la próxima semana en Bolonia, donde el equipo español tratará de reconquistar la Copa Davis liderado por el murciano. Para ese ansiado oro olímpico, que se escapó por poco en París 2024, habrá que esperar al menos hasta Los Ángeles 2028.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz scripts history, becomes just fourth Tennis player ever to achieve rare feat with ATP Finals win over Zverev
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz continued his winning run by defeating Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (7) in the ATP Finals championship match on Sunday, adding another title
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz continued his winning run by defeating Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (7) in the ATP Finals championship match on Sunday, adding another title to his season. The victory also kept alive questions over Zverev's inability to beat Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner during his breakout year.Alcaraz became the fourth player to win all four Grand Slam titles during his career and also lift the trophy at the season-ending tournament featuring the world's top eight players. Andre Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic are the other three players to have achieved the feat.“You’re an absolute legend of our sport and you’re only 23 years old,” Zverev said during his runner-up speech. “If you retire tomorrow, it’s OK, you can just relax.”Alcaraz overcomes injury concernsAlcaraz has been managing a left hamstring injury and played with a black elastic band around his upper thigh, along with tape around his right knee. He has continued to win matches despite the injury, having also missed four and a half months in the middle of the year because of a right wrist injury.The Spaniard extended his winning streak to 14 matches after winning titles in Vienna and Paris before the ATP Finals. His latest victory earned him a winner's cheque of almost $5.2 million.“It’s been an amazing week,” Alcaraz said. “I’ve been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team. ... I’m playing great tennis. So lifting the trophy is something I’ve (been) chasing for a really long time.”Zverev won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and reached the top of the world rankings for the first time this month. However, Alcaraz also defeated him in a five-set match in the Australian Open semifinals. That was their only other meeting this year, with the Spaniard now leading their career head-to-head record 8-6.Sinner has beaten Zverev in their last 10 meetings, including the Wimbledon final this year. However, the Italian ended his season early because of a right knee injury.Alcaraz breaks Zverev's serveZverev had not lost his serve throughout the tournament before the final, but Alcaraz put him under pressure in the opening game by earning three break points. Zverev saved all three, including one with an ace after receiving a time violation warning. However, Alcaraz broke his serve in each of his next three service games.Alcaraz controlled the match by moving Zverev from one corner of the court to the other. He also broke the German early in the second set.Zverev loses his cool after Alcaraz's tweenerZverev lost his temper midway through the first set after Alcaraz used a “tweener” — a shot played between the legs — to return a lob. Zverev missed the overhead that followed and threw his racket towards the baseline.On the next point, Zverev again took too long to serve and received a first-serve penalty. He then complained to the chair umpire.In the second set, Alcaraz produced an acrobatic overhead while falling backwards. He then pointed a finger towards his ear, asking the crowd to cheer louder.The match looked set to end quickly, but Zverev broke back to make it 4-4 in the second set. He then had three set points in the tiebreaker but failed to convert any of them. Alcaraz took his second match point with a backhand winner down the line.The Spaniard celebrated by dropping onto his back on the court.Alcaraz finished with 28 winners, more than twice Zverev's 12. articles.title: Chuva no Vale do Paraíba e Litoral: alagamentos e estragos na região | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporal deste domingo (22) provocou ocorrências em diferentes municípios. Sirene de alerta foi acionada em Campos do Jordão e moradores de Jambeiro enfrentaram alagamentos e lama dentro de casas.
articles.summary: Chuva no Vale do Paraíba e Litoral Norte causa alagamentos, queda de árvores e deixa rastro de lama em casas de Jambeiro e ruas de Ilhabela nesta segunda-feira.
articles.body:
As fortes chuvas que atingiram o Vale do Paraíba e o Litoral Norte neste domingo (22) provocaram alagamentos, queda de árvores, danos em vias públicas e transtornos para moradores de diferentes cidades da região.

Em Ubatuba, o temporal provocou alagamentos, transbordamento de rios, queda de árvores e deslizamentos, deixando famílias fora de casa e interditando vias. As aulas foram suspensas em três escolas municipais. Na manhã desta segunda, um corpo foi encontrado em um rio, mas ainda não há confirmação de que a morte tenha relação com a enchente - saiba mais clicando aqui.

Em Campos do Jordão , a sirene de alerta para chuvas intensas foi acionada durante a tarde. Segundo a Defesa Civil, o temporal provocou rajadas de vento, queda de granizo e de árvores.

Uma árvore tombou sobre uma quadra destruindo o alambrado e atingindo a testeira da sede Tênis Clube. Ninguém ficou ferido.

Árvore caiu após chuva forte no Tênis Clube, em Campos do Jordão — Foto: Márcio Correia

Ao longo do dia, alertas também foram enviados para outras cidades da região, incluindo Monteiro Lobato, Tremembé, São Bento do Sapucaí, São Luiz do Paraitinga, Aparecida, Guaratinguetá, Potim, Roseira, Cunha, Cruzeiro, Areias, Silveiras e Queluz.

Em Jambeiro , a vazão do rio que corta o bairro Tapanhão aumentou e a água invadiu casas próximas. Na manhã desta segunda-feira (23), moradores enfrentavam ruas tomadas pela lama e tentavam retirar a água e os resíduos que entraram nas residências.

Em nota, a Prefeitura afirmou que a força da água arrastou diversos materiais, como vegetação, bananeiras e pneus, que ficaram acumulados sob a ponte, impedindo "a adequada vazão do rio e provocando a elevação do nível da água, que acabou entrando no imóvel".

"Desde o primeiro momento, o município tomou todas as providências necessárias, mobilizando as equipes de Assistência Social, Saúde e, principalmente, trabalhadores, máquinas e equipamentos para a retirada dos materiais acumulados e a limpeza da área. A Prefeitura segue acompanhando a situação e prestando o apoio necessário, reafirmando seu compromisso com a segurança da população e o atendimento às famílias atingidas", concluiu.

Situação em Jambeiro após as chuvas deste domingo (22) — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Jambeiro

Já por volta das 21h, a Defesa Civil emitiu um alerta severo de chuva forte para Santa Isabel e Jacareí. A previsão indicava possibilidade de raios, ventos e granizo.

Em São José dos Campos , moradores registraram diversos raios durante a tempestade. A chuva também foi forte no Jardim Bandeirantes, na zona sul da cidade.

Ilhabela , por sua vez, registrou 83 milímetros de chuva neste domingo. De acordo com o balanço divulgado pela Defesa Civil na manhã desta segunda-feira (23) foram contabilizados três chamados envolvendo residências, dois problemas de infraestrutura e cinco pontos de alagamento em vias públicas.

No bairro Itaquanduba, um muro de pedra desabou na Rua Arapongas. Na Barra Velha, duas casas foram atingidas por alagamentos, nas ruas da Cachoeira e Salvador Arena.

Estragos causados pela chuva em Ilhabela — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Ilhabela

No Reino, houve solapamento da margem de um rio na Rua João Evangelista. Já no Morro do Cantagalo, o entupimento do sistema de drenagem provocou o arrastamento de materiais para a Rua Antônio Carlos dos Reis.

Também foram registrados pontos de alagamento nas ruas Maria Dias Barbosa e Benedito Rosa de Jesus e nas avenidas Princesa Isabel, na altura do Mercado Rosalina, São João e Pedro Paula de Moraes.

Equipes da Prefeitura realizam serviços de limpeza em diferentes pontos da cidade, com retirada de lama, resíduos e materiais arrastados pela chuva. A Defesa Civil segue monitorando as ocorrências e orienta moradores a evitar áreas alagadas e locais com risco de deslizamento.

articles.title: Four points to ponder after Carlos Alcaraz’s historic ATP Finals win
articles.summary: At 23, he is becoming a legend of the sport
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz won the ATP Finals for the first time. It is the 30th title of the 23-year-old Spaniard's career.

Tennis is better with Alcaraz in it, and the same could be said for Jannik Sinner who we hope to see healthy and in form again soon.

1. His resume is only missing 3 big individual titles

He has managed to win most of the biggest tournaments (Grand Slam and ATP 1000-level) of the sport. The only ones missing are the Canada Open. Shanghai Masters, and an Olympic gold medal.

Alcaraz is the fourth player to win the Career Slam and the ATP Finals. The other legends are Andre Agassi, Roger Federer, and Novak Djokovic. Alcaraz accomplished it at 23. Federer was 27, and Agassi and Djokovic were 29.

Many wondered the significance of "CCC" which is how Alcaraz signed the camera at the conclusion of the final. It translates to cabeza, corazon, and cojones. In English, that means head, heart, and balls, a phrase that his grandfather uses.

3. Tennis is a family affair for Alcaraz

Alcaraz's parents, Carlos and Virginia, brothers Alvaro and Jaime, and future sister-in-law (Alvaro's fiancee) Lucia, were in Turin and posed for family photos after thw win. His dad and Alvaro travel regularly with him on the ATP Tour. This title was extra special because more of the family was able to be there.

The plan for him is to join the Spanish Davis Cup team in Bologna, Italy as it faces Team Austria on November 26 in the quarterfinals. Team Spain has not won the Davis Cup during Alcaraz's pro career; their last win was in 2019.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz wins ATP Finals: Remarkable 84 days for Turin champion
articles.summary: Over the past 84 days, Carlos Alcaraz has won four titles, and he beat world number one Alexander Zverev to make history at the ATP Finals on Sunday.
articles.body:
The men's tennis season ended as it began, with a beaming Carlos Alcaraz holding aloft one of the sport's biggest trophies.

In January, he won the Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam. Ten months later, he stood as the victor in Turin, having ended his wait for a first ATP Finals title.

Watching Alcaraz over recent weeks, it would be easy to forget that for a four-month period this year, the 23-year-old barely picked up a racquet.

He missed the majority of the clay and all of the grass-court season with a wrist injury, but he has made a remarkable return, culminating in a dismantling of world number one Alexander Zverev on Sunday.

It is 84 days since Alcaraz made his comeback at the US Open, where his lack of match fitness understandably showed. He came through the early rounds but lost a five-set quarter-final epic against Ben Shelton.

Since then, the Spaniard has won 21 of his 22 matches - including each of the past 14 - and captured titles at four of the five tournaments he has contested.

He continues to make history, too, becoming the youngest man to win all four Slams and the season-ending Finals.

This was the third straight tournament he has won, following victories at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters earlier in November, and he has now won his past nine matches against fellow top-10 players.

The former world number one, currently ranked third behind Zverev and Jannik Sinner, continues to make up for lost time as he seeks to quickly reassert himself at the top of the sport.

"I think everybody feels he's the number one," Alcaraz said, stressing each player in the game has to treat themselves that way.

"Me, Sascha [Zverev], Jannik [Sinner], [Ben] Shelton. Having that confidence in yourself is really important.

"But right now the number one is Sascha. He really deserves it."

Crowd-pleasing variety, devastating power and astonishing athleticism did not take long to return to Alcaraz's game.

Even with a heavily strapped left leg after injuring his hamstring on Wednesday, he could not be stopped by the world's top players in Turin.

That included Zverev, who this year rose to the top of the rankings for the first time after claiming his first two major titles and recording a tour-leading 69 match wins.

Alcaraz, already a seven-time Slam winner, feels his own growth in the mental side of the sport has taken him to a different level in recent months.

He has specifically pointed to the new sense of perspective he gained from his time away from tennis in inspiring his scintillating year-end form.

"The injury made me realise what's really important," Alcaraz said.

"It's not winning. It's just about playing tennis. I realised that it is a gift every time that I can step on the court and compete healthy.

"When you realise that, everything comes easier.

"I don't feel stressed most of the time. I think right now I'm more mature, or I feel that, on a tennis court, I'm facing the problems and difficult moments in a different way."

Alcaraz threw himself to the ground after ending his wait to win the season-ending tournament before racing into the stands to celebrate with his team and family.

It marked the 30th title of his career, drawing him level with rival Sinner and behind only men's record 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic (102) among active ATP players.

More could soon be around the corner - should he manage to stay injury-free.

Victory in Paris has left him two titles away from emulating Sinner and Djokovic by completing the career 'Golden Masters' - winning all nine Masters 1,000 events, the level of tournament below the Slams.

Should he achieve that next season in Canada and Shanghai, it would leave him only an Olympic singles gold away from completing the sport.

His main obstacle to achieving such dominance still appears to be Sinner, given Alcaraz's positive head-to-head against Zverev.

Italian Sinner has been absent with a knee issue since Wimbledon but is aiming to return , external at the Australian Open, where Alcaraz will defend his title in January.

"In today's final, I needed to put the three Cs - cabeza, corazon, cojones - that my grandpa always tells me I have to give every time I step on the court," Alcaraz said.

"The three Cs in English is head, heart and balls. Today, that was what it was about.

"Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me."
